newsitem.title: USA: Peco Energy seeking to buy nuclear plants.
newsitem.headline: Peco Energy seeking to buy nuclear plants.

text.p: Peco Energy will continue to look for nuclear plants to purchase despite its failure to reach an agreement to buy the troubled Maine Yankee plant, a spokesman said Friday.

"Our efforts will continue. That is one of our business strategies for the future competition and deregulation," spokesman Bill Jones said in a telephone interview from Peco's Philadelphia headquarters.
Maine Yankee was the only plant under which Peco had active discussions, Jones said. "I'm sure we will look into other opportunities as they present themselves," he added.
Peco and Maine Yankee's current owners said they ended dicussions about a sale after both sides decided they could not reach an agreement that was financially beneficial to both sides.

Neither side would elaborate on what issues caused the talks to collapse. Maine Yankee's owner said they will now move to decommission the 25-year-old plant, which has been plagued by safety and equipment problems.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
